name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander (Australia)
description: Initial draft base profile for theses addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, knowledges and health. Aboriginal peoples and Torres Strait Islander peoples are distinct, and practices differ between nations, communities and regions; nation- or community-specific nuances belong in child profiles that extend this one. All entries require review by people with the relevant cultural authority before the profile is approved.

applies_to.notes: Add child profiles for specific nations, communities or regions where protocols differ.

concepts.label: Country
concepts.description: Relational connection to land, waters, sky and all they hold; not equivalent to 'land' as property.

concepts.label: Kinship
concepts.description: Systems of relationships, roles and obligations between people, and with Country.

concepts.label: Healing
concepts.description: Holistic restoration of wellbeing across physical, social, emotional, cultural and spiritual dimensions.

concepts.label: Social and emotional wellbeing
concepts.description: Holistic concept of health encompassing connections to body, mind, family, community, culture, Country and spirituality.

emphasised_topics.topic: Connection to Country, kin and culture in healing
emphasised_topics.rationale: Healing is understood relationally rather than solely at the individual level.

assessment_criteria.description: Evidence that communities were involved in shaping, governing and approving the research.
The researcher states their standpoint and relationship to the communities involved.
Methods are appropriate to the communities involved and justified with reference to Indigenous methodologies.
Consent processes and the governance, ownership and return of data and knowledge are addressed.
The research describes benefits to, and reciprocal relationships with, the communities involved.
Findings and discussion avoid deficit framing and recognise community strengths and knowledges.

research_question_framings.framing: Research aims or purposes defined with or by community

answer_guidance: Use the terminology and framing used by the thesis and its participants.
Recognise that wellbeing and healing may be described relationally, including connections to Country, kin, culture, community and spirituality.
Do not generalise practices from one community or nation to all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Avoid deficit framing; describe strengths where the source does.
Do not speculate about restricted, sacred or ceremonial knowledge.
